intro: Curtain rail and blind fitting is the secure installation of curtain hardware or blinds to a window or the wall surrounding it, and FixWell Services carries this out across Salisbury on standard windows, bay windows, and the solid masonry reveals common in the city's period properties. Call +44 7391 599 078 or use the quote form for a free quote.

sections.heading: What Curtain Rail & Blind Fitting Work FixWell Carries Out
sections.body: FixWell fits curtain poles and tracks, and recess or face-fix blinds, to standard windows, bay windows, and sash window reveals across Salisbury. Bracket spacing is calculated to the curtain's weight and the pole's span, not fitted at a fixed default distance, which is what prevents the sagging problem common with DIY fittings.

sections.heading: Fitting Curtain Rails and Blinds in Bay Windows
sections.body: A bay window needs a curved or multi-piece pole or track system rather than a single straight length, and the additional angles mean more fixing points are needed to support the curtain's weight across the wider span. Salisbury's Victorian bay-fronted terraces are where FixWell fits this kind of system most often, matching the pole's curve to the specific angle of each bay.

sections.heading: Fixing to Solid Masonry Window Reveals
sections.body: A masonry window reveal, common on the same period properties where FixWell also fits shelving, needs plugs sized to the curtain or blind's weight and a drill bit suited to stone or brick, since the wrong bit risks cracking the plaster finish around the reveal.

sections.heading: How FixWell Fits Curtain Rails and Blinds
sections.body: Every curtain or blind fitting starts with measuring the window and reveal precisely, then calculating bracket spacing based on the pole's span and the curtain's expected weight once fabric is hung. Fixings are placed and levelled before the pole or blind goes on, and the finished installation is tested by opening and closing curtains or raising and lowering a blind fully before the job is signed off.

sections.heading: Cost of Curtain Rail and Blind Fitting in Salisbury
sections.body: A standard single-window curtain pole or track fitting costs £30–£60. A bay window costs £60–£120, reflecting the extra brackets and the curved or multi-piece hardware involved. Blind fitting, whether recess or face-fix, costs £25–£50 per window. Combining a curtain or blind job with another small task in the same visit brings the effective cost down further.

sections.heading: Is Your Blind Manual, or Does It Need Power?
sections.body: A manual or battery-operated blind is a straightforward fitting job within FixWell's scope. A mains-wired motorised or smart blind needs power run to the window, which touches Part P electrical work and is covered under FixWell's electrical repairs service in Salisbury rather than this one.

sections.heading: Fitting Curtains and Blinds in a Rented Property
sections.body: A tenant should confirm with their landlord before any drilling into a window frame or reveal, and FixWell can fit reversible or minimal-fixing options where a landlord prefers the wall left undamaged at the end of a tenancy. This connects to FixWell's landlord property maintenance service in Salisbury.

sections.heading: Batching Curtain and Blind Fitting with Other Odd Jobs
sections.body: A minimum call-out charge applies to every booking, so fitting curtain rails and blinds alongside another small task in the same visit reduces the cost per job. FixWell's odd jobs page for Salisbury covers this batching approach in more detail.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to fit curtain rails in Salisbury?
faqs.a: £30–£60 for a standard single window, £60–£120 for a bay window. The bay window figure reflects the extra brackets and the curved or multi-piece pole system needed to follow the angle of the bay.

faqs.q: Can you fit blinds inside the window recess?
faqs.a: Yes. A recess-fit blind sits inside the window reveal for a neater finish; a face-fix blind mounts to the wall or frame surrounding the window where a recess isn't deep enough or doesn't exist.

faqs.q: Do you fit curtain poles in bay windows?
faqs.a: Yes, using a curved or multi-piece pole matched to the specific angle of the bay, with bracket spacing calculated for the wider span involved.

faqs.q: Can you fit blinds in a rented property without damaging the frame?
faqs.a: Yes. Reversible or minimal-fixing options are available where a landlord prefers the window frame left without permanent drilling, and FixWell will confirm the approach before starting.

faqs.q: Do you fit electric or smart blinds?
faqs.a: Manual and battery-operated blinds, yes. Mains-wired motorised blinds need power routed to the window, which is electrical work covered separately under FixWell's electrical repairs service.
